theory.intro: A **composite prism** has the same cross-section all the way through, but that cross-section is made of simpler shapes fitted together, such as an L-shape or a house-end pentagon. The rule $V = Ah$ still applies, with $A$ the area of the whole cross-section.
facts: **$V = Ah$**, where $A$ is the area of the uniform cross-section and $h$ is the length (perpendicular distance) through the prism.
Cross-section area formulas: rectangle $A = lw$, triangle $A = \frac{bh}{2}$, trapezium $A = \frac{h(a+b)}{2}$.
Every area uses the **perpendicular** height of the shape, never a slant side.
Multiply by the length of the prism, not by the perimeter of the cross-section.
A length in cm and an area in cm² give a volume in cm³.
steps: Dissect the cross-section into rectangles and triangles.
Find the total cross-sectional area by adding or subtracting the parts.
Multiply the cross-sectional area by the length of the prism.

workedExamples.solution_text:
Find the cross-sectional area using the parallel sides and perpendicular depth.
$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{0.8(2+1.2)}{2}\\&=1.28\text{ m}^2\\V&=Ah\\&=1.28\times5\\&=6.4\text{ m}^3\end{align*}$
Convert the volume to litres.
$\begin{align*}C&=6.4\times1000\\&=6400\text{ L}\end{align*}$
Divide the capacity by the filling rate.
$\begin{align*}t&=\frac{6400}{200}\\&=32\text{ minutes}\end{align*}$

Subtract the notch area from the full rectangle area, then multiply by the prism length.
$\begin{align*}A&=(9\times7)-(3\times2)\\&=63-6\\&=57\text{ cm}^2\\V&=Ah\\&=57\times8\\&=456\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$

Find the rectangle and trapezium areas separately, then add them.
$\begin{align*}A_1&=10\times5\\&=50\text{ mm}^2\\A_2&=\frac{9(10+18)}{2}\\&=126\text{ mm}^2\\A&=50+126\\&=176\text{ mm}^2\\V&=Ah\\&=176\times20\\&=3520\text{ mm}^3\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A concrete beam has a uniform composite cross-section of area $0.32\text{ m}^2$ and a length of $7.5\text{ m}$. Find the volume of concrete in the beam.

foundation.solution_text:
The cross-section is a trapezium with parallel sides $10$ cm and $6$ cm and perpendicular height $4$ cm.
$A = \frac{4(10 + 6)}{2}$
$= 32\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 32 \times 9$
$= 288\text{ cm}^{3}$

foundation.question_text:
An L-shaped prism has a bottom rectangle $8\text{ cm}$ wide and $2\text{ cm}$ high, with an upright column $3\text{ cm}$ wide reaching a total height of $7\text{ cm}$. The cross-section is uniform along its $6\text{ cm}$ length.
Find the volume, in $\text{cm}^3$.
foundation.solution_text:
Split the L-shaped cross-section into two rectangles.
$A = (8 \times 2) + (3 \times 5)$
$= 16 + 15$
$= 31\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 31 \times 6$
$= 186\text{ cm}^{3}$

development.solution_text:
The uniform cross-section is the trapezium-shaped side wall.
$A = \frac{20(1 + 2.5)}{2}$
$= 35\text{ m}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 35 \times 10$
$= 350\text{ m}^{3}$
Capacity $= 350 \times 1000$
$= 350\,000\text{ L}$

development.question_text:
An L-shaped prism has a bottom rectangle $9.5\text{ cm}$ wide and $2.4\text{ cm}$ high, with an upright column $3.2\text{ cm}$ wide reaching a total height of $7.9\text{ cm}$. The prism is $8.5\text{ cm}$ long.
Find its volume, in $\text{cm}^3$, to $1$ decimal place.
development.solution_text:
Split the L-shaped cross-section into two rectangles.
$A = (9.5 \times 2.4) + (3.2 \times 5.5)$
$= 22.8 + 17.6$
$= 40.4\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 40.4 \times 8.5$
$= 343.4\text{ cm}^{3}$

development.question_text:
A prism has a uniform cross-section made of a $12$ cm by $5$ cm rectangle with a right-angled triangle of base $12$ cm and height $4$ cm sitting on top of it (a house-shaped pentagon).
The prism is $7$ cm long.
Find its volume, in cm³.

A T-shaped concrete beam has a uniform cross-sectional area of $0.45$ m² and is $6$ m long.
Find the volume of concrete in the beam, in m³.

A ramp is a prism with a uniform cross-section whose vertical sides are $2.3\text{ m}$ and $4.8\text{ m}$, separated horizontally by $7.2\text{ m}$. The bottom is horizontal and the top slopes between the vertical sides. The ramp is $3.5\text{ m}$ wide.
Find its volume, in $\text{m}^3$, to $1$ decimal place.
development.solution_text:
Split the cross-section into a rectangle and a triangle.
$A = (7.2 \times 2.3) + \frac{7.2 \times (4.8 - 2.3)}{2}$
$= 16.56 + 9$
$= 25.56\text{ m}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 25.56 \times 3.5$
$= 89.46\text{ m}^{3}$
$\approx 89.5\text{ m}^{3}$

development.question_text:
A prism has a uniform cross-section made of a rectangle $9\text{ mm}$ wide and $6\text{ mm}$ high on top of a trapezium. The trapezium has a top width of $9\text{ mm}$, a bottom width of $16\text{ mm}$ and a perpendicular height of $8\text{ mm}$. The prism is $24\text{ mm}$ long.
Find its volume, in $\text{mm}^3$.
development.solution_text:
Split the cross-section into the rectangle and the trapezium.
$A = (9 \times 6) + \frac{8(9 + 16)}{2}$
$= 54 + 100$
$= 154\text{ mm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 154 \times 24$
$= 3696\text{ mm}^{3}$

mastery.question_text:
An embankment is a prism whose uniform cross-section is a $12$ m by $4$ m rectangle with a trapezium on top, the trapezium having parallel sides $12$ m and $6$ m and a height of $3$ m. The embankment is $8$ m long.
Find the volume of earth in it, in m³.
mastery.solution_text:
Split the cross-section into the rectangle and the trapezium.
$A = (12 \times 4) + \frac{3(12 + 6)}{2}$
$= 48 + 27$
$= 75\text{ m}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 75 \times 8$
$= 600\text{ m}^{3}$

mastery.question_text:
A pool shell has a level top and is $28\text{ m}$ long and $11\text{ m}$ wide. Its uniform side cross-section has a horizontal floor at a depth of $2.6\text{ m}$ for the first $7\text{ m}$, then a floor that slopes upwards to a depth of $1.4\text{ m}$ at the other end.
Find the volume of earth that must be excavated for the shell to fit exactly, in $\text{m}^3$.
mastery.solution_text:
Split the side cross-section into a rectangle and a trapezium.
The sloping section is $28 - 7 = 21\text{ m}$ long.
$A = (7 \times 2.6) + \frac{21(2.6 + 1.4)}{2}$
$= 18.2 + 42$
$= 60.2\text{ m}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 60.2 \times 11$
$= 662.2\text{ m}^{3}$

mastery.question_text:
A water trough is a prism whose cross-section is a trapezium with parallel sides $2$ m (top) and $1.2$ m (bottom) and a depth of $0.6$ m; the trough is $3.5$ m long.
Water flows in at $280$ litres per minute.
Using $1$ m³ $= 1000$ L, find how many minutes it takes to fill the trough.
